brief: Two gates in this loop are not telling the truth, and both are cheap. FIRST, the memory budget. context-budget.mjs has read OVER on twenty-five consecutive worker opens and has been reset by five manager passes; it is advisory, so a worker reads it, writes 'OVER 50.2 of 46 KB' into its ledger entry, and ships. The total is not something a worker can fix - but what ONE iteration ADDS is. Give the tool a second mode that reports an iteration's own additions against a quota (one ledger entry <= 1.8 KB, at most one inventory line <= 250 B, at most one cue <= 250 B, merging otherwise), prints the offending lines, and is non-zero when they are exceeded, so the worker's log step can hold it. SECOND, c227: probes/punt.mjs reports a stranding for every night rider, because its test is 'a.eyot after eastOpen() closed' and #131's eastOpenFor() legitimately covers that case. It has cried wolf on HEAD since #141. Fix its test or retire it.
successLooksLike: context-budget.mjs --additions exits non-zero on a staged over-quota inventory line and names it, and zero on HEAD. probes/punt.mjs passes on HEAD and can still be shown to FAIL on a build that really strands a night rider.
avoid: Do not change the 46 KB cap or the 12 KB laws cap - changing a cap mid-run is how a loop stops noticing. Do not make the total budget block a worker: it is the manager's number, and a worker cannot fix it inside its own iteration. And do not retire the punt gate without showing the test it replaces can still go red.
